summary: Add a nullable boolean column marketing_opt_in to account_user with DEFAULT false, backfill existing rows to false, deploy the new version with a state‑only migration, retire the old version, then alter the column to NOT NULL. The DEFAULT false ensures the old version’s INSERT statements omit the column and still get a valid value, keeping writes consistent during the overlap.
write_consistency: The column DEFAULT false causes the old version’s INSERT (which omits unknown columns) to set marketing_opt_in to false, so no NULLs appear from the old version. The new version explicitly writes the column; concurrent reads see the most recent write from either version.

stages.description: Add nullable boolean column marketing_opt_in with DEFAULT false
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN marketing_opt_in boolean DEFAULT false;

stages.description: Set marketing_opt_in to false for any rows that currently have NULL
sql: UPDATE account_user SET marketing_opt_in = false WHERE marketing_opt_in IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version; after this only the new version serves traffic

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN marketing_opt_in SET NOT NULL;
